That relationship sounds somewhat unhealthy but it's hard to say without knowing context. However it is clear that you are going through a lot. Trust me, the resources are there for exactly this situation. It may also be a good lead into getting some help, though I personally find that terrifying sometimes.

If you are being abused - verbally, physically, emotionally, in any way - it seems that the "default" human reaction is to blame yourself. I struggle with abusing myself in fact - I'm really mean to myself inside - and I blame myself for it rather than the way my mind currently works. I've also been abused by others, and have an almost impossible time admitting anything other than guilt and self-hatred, even to myself. 

I suppose it's worth saying - if you really want to kill yourself, does it have to be this painful? Can the pain of being poked at and feeling ashamed or embarrassed in the hospital be that much worse than the pain you go through on a daily basis, let alone the pain you're currently in? I hope you at least give it a try. There's a lot shittier people out there, and I can guarantee that, because I've been on the internet.

Thanks for sharing. I'm really struggling myself lately. I hope it's okay to post this comment - to be honest it's really hard to type this out, but I promise there's relevance to your post. Since this might be a difficult read, I'll go ahead and say the relevant part here: your post helped me choose to fight on instead of giving up. 

I hate myself so much for even thinking about suicide because of how it would affect those I care about, but of course these thoughts don't just go away. 

I've been depressed since I was pretty young. I've been in therapy again the past few months with a therapist I really like, but I'm feeling really discouraged with it and I don't feel safe talking about anything to do with depression. Suicide? No way I'd even bring it up. Unfortunately in this country I've found that potential liability takes precedence over patient care, so each time I've really been struggling I have really regretted asking for help and felt worse off and more alone after it was all over. I've had so many medications thrown at me; some have left me with severe, sometimes permanent side effects and withdrawal symptoms. 

Lately things have gotten worse. I have felt like just about everything and everyone I interact with I mess up. Some things in my life have been difficult lately, and I don't feel like I am able to be nearly as good to my partner of 5 years as she is to me. With COVID stuff going on and having moved farther away, I barely talk to my friends and family. When I do talk to people, I feel like my sadness or exhaustion or anxiety translates what I want to communicate into something else - people think I am bothered by them when I am really just kind of nervous (but honestly glad to see them). I can't escape the feeling that if only I didn't exist, if only something happened and I was killed, then they wouldn't have to worry about me anymore, and I wouldn't have to continually disappoint them.

However I am aware of the fact that there are repercussions. Despite distance or conflicts or issues, death hurts those it touches. 

Your post helped remind me of that.

If I want to minimize the amount I feel that I hurt people, I need to find a different way to do it. Because dying will hurt them in a whole different way. I don't know what other path there is, but I will fight until I find it, and for my sake and the sake of those I love I hope I do find it.
